newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-MMI says sees strong result in 1997.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-MMI says sees strong result in 1997.

text.p: Insurance group MMI Ltd said on Thursday it was on track to deliver a strong result for the full 1996/97 financial year ending June 30.

"Given the current investment earnings and continued improvement in our core businesses, we are on track to deliver a strong result in the 1997 financial year," the company said after annoucing half year results.
The company also said it expected to make some further announcements about its progress in Asia in the near future.
"The soft market rates are expected to continue throughout 1997," MMI managing director Pieter Franzen said.
"Barring further natural disasters, the high level of claims in the first half should abate, with benefits to the underwriting result," he said.
MMI, 38 percent owned by Germany's Allianz AG, earlier reported a half year net profit of A$18.08 million, up from A$15.11 million a year earlier.
Franzen said the result was very positive when viewed in the context of softening rates in the insurance market and the increase in short-term claim experienced during the period.
The profit result reflected the early benefits of the company's substantial investment in process improvements, technology and strategic initiatives, he said.

Franzen said the investment portfolio made a strong contribution to the result with the total for realised and unrealised gains up 23.5 percent, from A$61.2 million to A$75.6 million, compared with a year earlier.
Both fixed interest and equity investments benefited from the strength of international and Australian markets, he said.

Franzen said the savings forecast from process improvements and the company's expense containment strategies were beginning to flow through. "Expenses continued their downward trend from 15.0 percent as at June 30 1996 to 13.5 percent in December 1996. Expense management remains a priority for MMI," he said.

Rates in the commercial insurance market were very soft, Franzen said. Despite this, the Marine and Industrial Special Risk portfolios were ahead of budget, and MMI maintained its leading position in Workers Compensation, with a national market share in excess of 20 percent, he said.
Gross written premium for packaged business insurance, targeted at small-to-medium business, increased 11.7 percent compared with a year earlier.
In family insurance, gross written premium rose seven percent after a strong performance of Club Marine and improvements in the New South Wales compulsory third party portfolio.
However, claims were unexpectedly high as a result of storms ine Armidale and Singleton, New South Wales, and floods at Coffs Harbour, New South Wales.
This put pressure on the underwriting result but was off-set by higher investment returns, Franzen said.
Franzen said MMI continuing to make significant and tangible progress on expanding the mix and geographic spread of its business, in line with the strategic plan announced in May 1995.
MMI is in the process of acquiring 20 percent of Allianz Insurance (Singapore) Pte Ltd and this should be completed by March 31 1997, he added.
